correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the transition identity d(bk+r)=0 at r=0..b-3, 1 at r=b-2, and 1 or 0 at r=b-1 depending on parent-letter equality. Every b-window of the coded transition string 0^(b-2)1e has unique residue phase for b>=3: a single 1 is mandatory, while two 1s identify the mandatory one as first of adjacent pair or last of endpoint pair. Circular (b+1)-windows occur when n>=b+2, so phase increments round the circle force b|n. For n=bm, an aligned circular word decomposes uniquely into mu_b-blocks; rotating one symbol into each block enforces each length-(m+1) periodic source extension and proves both surjection and injection. Short n<=b+1 classification follows from maximal constant-run lengths 1,b-1,b and absence of four-letter alternation, plus explicit base-3 length-four factor enumeration. The three source classes 00,01,11 generate distinct surviving length-2b^k images using 000,010,101,111 source triples and the imbalance (b-2)^k. Independently regenerated fixed points, checked all phases at b=3..8 and Lie values/extension equivalence at n=1..50, plus b=3,4 at n=2b^3; these finite tests corroborate but do not establish all b,n. No nonstandard lemma remains unproved within the stated elementary phase/run argument.

value.rationale: Lie complexity is a natural conjugacy-sensitive invariant of automatic-word languages, strictly different from square counts or Abelian factor counts. The all-base sharp divisibility support and one-symbol source-window bijection settle a motivated infinite structural question, with exceptional boundary b+1, nontrivial mixed class at 2b and an infinite family of nonzero multiples. These nontrivial restrictions are not mechanical consequences of recognizability alone, automaticity or known square spectra. No full numeric formula at all multiples or paper-sized extension is required.

final_claim: For every integer b>=3, L_b(1)=2,L_b(2)=3,L_b(n)=4 (3<=n<=b),L_b(b+1)=3 for b=3 or 2 for b>=4; if n>=b+2 and b does not divide n, L_b(n)=0; at each n=bm,m>=2, the rotation-complete conjugacy classes are exactly mu_b-images of circular length-m words whose every periodic source window of length m+1 occurs in w_b; L_b(2b)=3 and L_b(2b^k)>=3 for every k>=1. No numeric closed formula at arbitrary surviving lengths is claimed.
limitations: The result is an exact classification via E_b(m), not a simplified formula for all surviving multiples. Base b=2 excluded: the phase code loses uniqueness.

Kishi 2026 already provides base-three strong interference-freeness and circular recognizability, which are materially credited; the remaining Lie-specific support and extension comparison is best-of-knowledge.
